top_story: The ICJ’s 19 November genocide finding against Myanmar has sharpened the legal and political stakes around mass-atrocity cases, especially as fears of possible US sanctions on judges signal a push to intimidate international judicial scrutiny before future rulings touching Israel and Gaza. That pressure lands as violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank remains embedded in daily life, underscored by the 17 November killing of 72-year-old Fadha Wadha near Jericho, where settler attacks deepen insecurity far from the Gaza battlefield. The 18 November US sentencing of a Pakistani man for a plot tied to revenge for Qassem Suleimani’s killing also revives the shadow of Iran-linked transnational retaliation, reinforcing how unresolved regional conflicts continue to spill across legal, diplomatic, and civilian arenas. The emerging picture is of a region and its wider international environment in which accountability mechanisms are gaining force just as states and armed networks intensify efforts to deter, bypass, or violently answer them.
